newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends sharply lower, under pressure.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends sharply lower, under pressure.

text.p: COMEX copper ended sharply down, barely off the day's low and vulnerable to more downward pressure, despite a potentially major strike in at Kennecott Copper in Utah, traders said.
Mike Frawley of Dean Witter Reynolds said it was not a good sign that the market was falling at a time of a possible strike at the 310,000 short tons per year smelter.
Three days of talks have been set aside since Tuesday to resolve the deadlock in Kennecott's labor negotiations for a new contract. The previous contract expired September 30.

"It's another indication that there is a lot of metal out there which Sumitomo is probably unwinding," Frawley said. "Physical business in the U.S. has been good but there are some signs that it's beginning to slow a little bit."

Traders noted some earlier fund selling which triggered sell stops, but saw some support at 88.00 cents basis December COMEX, which settled 1.95 cents lower at 88.65 cents per pound, traded 91.30 to 88.55 cents.
LME also slumped in evening trade after failing to make headway on the upside, hitting resistance at $1,950 a tonne.
